articles.title: CHUNK-PEZESHKIAN-BRICS-BUSINESS-FORUM
articles.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has urged BRICS to construct resilient economic systems capable of protecting its members and the wider Global South from sanctions, military pressure and disruptions to legitimate trade. Speaking at the BRICS gathering in New Delhi, Pezeshkian said recent American and Israeli military action against Iran demonstrated that economic security cannot be separated from national or regional security. He warned that pressure on a country’s trade, energy infrastructure and financial system can spread across borders and destabilise the global economy. Pezeshkian called on BRICS to reduce dependence on monopolised financial and technological instruments that can be used to obstruct another country’s commerce.

articles.title: On cam: Trump defends $5000 Biden 'reward' plan, says it will be funded by 'tremendous' growth
articles.description: Donald Trump defended his proposed $5,000 dividend for every adult American, insisting “tremendous” U.S. economic growth would provide enough money to finance the payments. Pressed over America's $40 trillion national debt and the potential impact on the deficit, Trump said he was “not at all worried” and argued Americans deserved the money after enduring Biden-era policies. The President also denied tying the proposal to voter turnout, despite making Republican control of Congress a condition for the payout. With the plan potentially costing $1.3 trillion, can Trump's growth gamble really pay for the checks?

articles.title: In 1905, Bengaluru’s streets went electric; the power came from Shivanasamudra, a hydro plant built to power Kolar’s gold mines
articles.description: Bengaluru's streets became illuminated with electric lights in 1905. Power for these lights originated from the Shivanasamudra hydroelectric project. This project initially supplied electricity to the Kolar Gold Fields for mining operations. The electricity network later expanded to include domestic consumers in the city. This development marked an early stage in Bengaluru's electrification.
